asA: beta reader relying on the referee-guarantees page to know what `rcf define validate` proves
iWant: a broken ADR supersededBy pointer to be reported as a brokenReference the same way a broken parent link is, and the soft `relatedAdrs` back-reference to stay silent so the ratified blueprint-supersede workflow is not broken
soThat: the docs-page promise that every reference in every document resolves is enforced on the strong chain-of-decisions reference (supersededBy), while the soft see-also field stays a schemas follow-up (either value-narrowed or workflow-aware)
title: US-16301: define validate walks ADR supersededBy; relatedAdrs stays a schemas follow-up (compatibility carry)

acceptanceCriteria.description: An ADR whose supersededBy names an id with no file on disk (or an id that resolves to a non-ADR kind) surfaces as a brokenReference error naming the ADR file and the field `supersededBy`, and the corresponding target id joins tree.brokenIds. A supersededBy field that is absent or empty is silent.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an initialised RCF project with adr-001.json whose supersededBy is set to a non-existent id ADR-999
acceptanceCriteria.when: walkTree runs (as invoked by `rcf define validate`)
acceptanceCriteria.then: errors contain a brokenReference with documentId ADR-001 and field supersededBy naming ADR-999, and tree.brokenIds contains ADR-999

acceptanceCriteria.description: An ADR whose relatedAdrs contains an id with no file on disk stays SILENT under walkTree: the ratified `rcf define blueprint supersede` workflow writes a project ADR whose relatedAdrs lists both the applied blueprint ADR (on disk) and the incoming blueprint ADR (not yet on disk; the incoming add is the closing step of option 3). Walking relatedAdrs would refuse that workflow between the supersede write and the re-add; the compatibility carry keeps the soft back-reference unchecked here. Tightening this is a schemas follow-up (value-narrow to applied ADR ids, or a workflow-aware exception on the supersede write path).
acceptanceCriteria.given: an initialised RCF project with adr-001.json whose relatedAdrs is set to [ADR-777] (a non-existent id, mirroring the transient state between supersede and re-add)
acceptanceCriteria.when: walkTree runs (as invoked by `rcf define validate`)
acceptanceCriteria.then: no brokenReference error targets the relatedAdrs field on ADR-001
